name: Karma-yoga: performing one's duty without attachment to the fruit
method_summary: BhG 4–6: do the action that is to be done without depending on its fruit (6.1), abandoning attachment and the fruit (4.20, 5.12), placing actions in Brahman (5.10), acting with body, mind, intellect and senses for purification of the self (5.11), for the sake of sacrifice (4.23), as the ancient seekers of liberation did (4.15). Declared superior to the renunciation of action (5.2).
stage: the means for the sage wishing to ascend to yoga (6.3)
signs_of_progress: not stained by sin though acting, like a lotus leaf by water (5.10)

warnings.text: The unyoked one, attached to the fruit through the drive of desire, is bound (5.12).

name: Sacrifice performed as duty (yajña)
method_summary: BhG 4: result-seekers sacrifice to the deities for quick success (4.12); action done for the sake of sacrifice dissolves (4.23); those who eat the nectar-remainder of sacrifice go to the eternal Brahman, and not even this world is for the non-sacrificer (4.31); the many sacrifices are all born of action (4.32).

name: Offering as Brahman (brahmārpaṇa)
method_summary: BhG 4.24: performing the offering while the act or instrument of offering, the oblation, the fire, the offerer and the goal are all Brahman — absorption in action as Brahman (brahma-karma-samādhi).

name: Sacrifice to the gods (daiva yajña)
method_summary: BhG 4.25: some yogins attend to sacrifice to the gods alone; cf. 4.12, people desiring success of their actions sacrifice to the deities, and success born of action comes quickly in the human world.

name: Offering sacrifice by sacrifice into the fire of Brahman
method_summary: BhG 4.25: others offer sacrifice by means of sacrifice itself into the fire of Brahman. The verse gives no further detail (commentators read it as offering the self into Brahman, or the sacrificial act itself).

name: Offering the senses into the fires of restraint
method_summary: BhG 4.26: offering the senses, beginning with hearing, into the fires of restraint (saṃyama) — sense-restraint described as a fire-offering.

name: Offering sense objects into the fires of the senses
method_summary: BhG 4.26: offering the sense objects, beginning with sound, into the fires of the senses — the senses' taking of their objects described as a fire-offering.

name: The fire of the yoga of self-restraint (ātma-saṃyama-yoga)
method_summary: BhG 4.27: offering all the activities of the senses and the activities of the vital breath into the fire of the yoga of self-restraint, kindled by knowledge.

name: Sacrifice with material things (dravya-yajña)
method_summary: BhG 4.28: sacrifice with material things, one of the forms of sacrifice; 4.33: the sacrifice of knowledge is better than sacrifice made of material things.

name: Austerity (tapas)
method_summary: BhG 4.28: austerity offered as sacrifice (tapo-yajña); 4.10: many have been purified by the austerity of knowledge (jñāna-tapas). 6.46 ranks the yogin above the ascetics (tapasvin).

name: Self-study (svādhyāya)
method_summary: BhG 4.28: ascetics of strict vows offer study/recitation (svādhyāya) together with knowledge as sacrifice.

name: The sacrifice of knowledge (jñāna-yajña)
method_summary: BhG 4.28, 4.33–34: offering knowledge as sacrifice; better than material sacrifice, since all action culminates in knowledge; the knowledge is learned from knowers who have seen the truth, approached with prostration, questioning and service.
prerequisites: faith, intentness and restraint of the senses (4.39)
signs_of_progress: freedom from delusion; seeing all beings in the self and in the Lord (4.35)

name: Breath as sacrifice: offering prāṇa and apāna
method_summary: BhG 4.29: offering prāṇa into apāna and apāna into prāṇa, and, restraining the movements of both, being devoted to breath-regulation. 4.30: others with regulated food offer the breaths into the breaths. The verses give no counts or durations.

name: Breath-regulation (prāṇāyāma)
method_summary: BhG 4.29: those devoted to prāṇāyāma restrain the movements of prāṇa and apāna, as one of the forms of sacrifice. No method beyond this is given in the chunk.

name: Regulated food with offering of the breaths (niyatāhāra)
method_summary: BhG 4.30: some, regulating their food, offer the vital breaths into the vital breaths, as a form of sacrifice.
notes: The meaning of 'offering prāṇas into prāṇas' is not spelled out in the verse.

name: Approaching the teacher: prostration, inquiry and service
method_summary: BhG 4.34: learn knowledge through prostration (praṇipāta), repeated questioning (paripraśna) and service (sevā); the knowers who have seen the truth will teach it.
signs_of_progress: no further delusion; seeing all beings in the self and in the Lord (4.35)

name: 'I do nothing at all' — the knower's contemplation of non-agency
method_summary: BhG 5.8–9: the yoked knower of reality thinks 'I do nothing at all' while seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, walking, sleeping, breathing, speaking, releasing, grasping and blinking, holding that it is the senses that move among the objects of the senses.
stage: the yoked knower of reality (yukta, tattvavit)

name: Fixing the gaze between the eyebrows
method_summary: BhG 5.27: with external contacts put outside, the gaze (cakṣus) is placed between the brows, while prāṇa and apāna are made equal; given only in outline.

name: Making prāṇa and apāna equal (BhG 5.27–28)
method_summary: BhG 5.27–28: putting the external contacts outside, placing the gaze between the brows, making equal the prāṇa and apāna that move within the nostrils; the sage with senses, mind and intellect restrained, intent on liberation, free of desire, fear and anger. Outline only; no counts or durations.
signs_of_progress: such a sage is ever liberated (5.28)

name: The Gītā's meditation (dhyāna-yoga, BhG 6.10–32)
method_summary: BhG 6.10–28: the yogin constantly yokes himself, in a secluded place, alone, restrained in mind and self, without expectations or possessions (6.10); sets a firm seat in a clean place (6.11); makes the mind one-pointed and practises for self-purification (6.12); holds body, head and neck in line, gaze toward the nose-tip (6.13); calm, fearless, firm in the brahmacārin's vow, mind restrained and fixed on the Lord, intent on him (6.14); moderate in food, recreation, effort, sleep and waking (6.16–17); abandons desires born of intention, restrains the senses by the mind, comes to rest little by little by the intellect held in steadfastness, makes the mind abide in the self and thinks of nothing (6.24–25); brings the wandering mind back each time (6.26).
stage: for one ascended to yoga calm is the means (6.3–4); practised constantly (6.10, 6.15, 6.28)
prerequisites: solitude, restraint, no expectations or possessions (6.10)
a clean place and a firm seat (6.11)
the vow of the brahmacārin; fearlessness (6.14)
signs_of_progress: the mind rests in the self alone, free of craving (6.18)
like a lamp in a windless place (6.19)
the stilled mind comes to rest; seeing the self by the self; boundless happiness beyond the senses; not shaken by heavy sorrow (6.20–22)
the highest happiness, contact with Brahman (6.27–28)
seeing the self in all beings and all beings in the self (6.29)
peace culminating in nirvāṇa, abiding in the Lord (6.15)

warnings.text: Yoga is not for one who eats too much or not at all, sleeps too much or keeps awake too long (6.16).
The mind is restless and wanders; it must be brought back each time (6.26); it is held by practice and dispassion (6.35).
Yoga is hard to attain for one whose self is unrestrained (6.36).

name: The meditation seat and posture of the Gītā
method_summary: BhG 6.11–13: in a clean place, a firm seat of one's own, neither too high nor too low, covered with cloth, deerskin and kuśa grass; sitting on it with body, head and neck held in line and motionless, steady, gaze toward the tip of the nose, not looking about.

name: Gaze toward the tip of the nose (nāsikāgra)
method_summary: BhG 6.13: in the meditation posture, looking toward the tip of one's own nose and not looking about in the directions (some commentators: 'as if' looking, the attention held within).

name: The vow of the brahmacārin (brahmacarya)
method_summary: BhG 6.14: the meditator is to be firm in the vow of the brahmacārin (brahmacāri-vrata). The verse does not spell out the vow.

name: Moderation in food, recreation and sleep (yuktāhāra-vihāra)
method_summary: BhG 6.16–17: yoga is for one measured in food and recreation, in effort in actions, in sleep and waking — not for one who eats too much or not at all, or sleeps too much or keeps awake too long.
signs_of_progress: yoga becomes the destroyer of suffering (6.17)

warnings.text: Yoga is not for one who eats too much, nor for one who does not eat at all, nor for one who sleeps too much or stays awake too long (6.16).

name: Practice and dispassion (abhyāsa and vairāgya)
method_summary: BhG 6.35–36: the restless mind, hard to restrain, is held by practice and dispassion; yoga is attainable by the self-controlled who strive through the right means; 6.26: whenever the mind wanders it is brought back to the self; 6.44: former practice carries one on in a later birth.

name: Seeing all by likeness to oneself (ātmaupamya)
method_summary: BhG 6.32: seeing the same everywhere, pleasure or pain, by likeness to oneself — the mark of the highest yogin.
